## What you will be able to do

::: {.mm-outcomes-wrap}
- Explain the difference between Linux, a terminal and Bash.
- Navigate a project using relative and absolute paths, including filenames with spaces.
- Inspect, copy, rename and remove practice files while preserving the raw inputs.
- Read permissions and choose the intended Python interpreter.
- Run a script, separate its results from its diagnostics and recognise a failed command.
- Inspect a process and manage a small job in your own terminal.
:::

## Lab

{{< generated ch16-labs >}}

Build a small analysis workspace, keep an unchanged raw-data copy, produce a sample-count report and recover from an incorrect path. The lab runs without network access after you open the notebook; its tiny synthetic dataset is embedded in the setup cell.

Finish with the [chapter checkpoint](checkpoint.html), then use the [key points](key-points.html) as a reference beside your terminal.

## Before you start

::: {.prereq}
No earlier machine learning chapter is required. Follow the [Linux & Bash setup instructions](../index.html) to prepare a Bash terminal and the practice files. The examples use a project directory called `mm-linux-lab`, with input files under `data/raw/`. Windows learners should use a Linux terminal in WSL for the lessons; the notebook lab also supports Git Bash.
:::

::: {.bridge audience="bio"}
Treat a project directory like the labelled container for an experiment: raw measurements, processing instructions and derived results each have a place. Knowing which container you are in is the first step towards knowing what your analysis actually used.
:::
